{
  "decision": "APPLY",
  "workflow_yaml": "# This workflow will build a Java project with Gradle
# For more information see: https://help.github.com/actions/language-and-framework-guides/building-and-testing-java-with-gradle

name: BTrace CI/CD

on:
  push:
    branches: [ develop ]
  pull_request:
    branches: [ develop ]
  # Required checks must also report on the merge queue's groups, or the queue drops every entry
  merge_group:
  workflow_dispatch:

defaults:
  run:
    shell: bash

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Set up Java 24
        uses: actions/setup-java@b843ebf9b913146b38da2eaa7aeddf76074ae1ad # v6
        with:
          java-version: 24
          distribution: temurin
      - name: Set up Java 28 (EA, runs the ClassFile API backend tests on version-72 class files)
        uses: actions/setup-java@b843ebf9b913146b38da2eaa7aeddf76074ae1ad # v6
        with:
          java-version: 28-ea
          distribution: temurin
      - name: Set up Java
        uses: actions/setup-java@b843ebf9b913146b38da2eaa7aeddf76074ae1ad # v6
        with:
          java-version: 21
          distribution: temurin
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7
      - name: Grant execute permission for gradlew
        run: chmod +x gradlew
      - name: Setup Gradle
        uses: gradle/actions/setup-gradle@8da46b539cd8fe6ab27ca75128919a18d757604c # v6
      - name: Generate cache key
        id: cache-key
        run: |
          key="${{ runner.os }}-gradle-1-${{ hashFiles('**/*.gradle*', '**/gradle-wrapper.properties') }}"
          echo "key=${key}" >> $GITHUB_ENV
          echo "cache-key=${key}" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
      - name: Cache Gradle
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6
        with:
          path: ~/.gradle/caches
          key: ${{ env.key }}
          restore-keys: |
            ${{ runner.os }}-gradle-
      - name: Build
        run: ./gradlew --no-daemon --parallel --build-cache build
      - name: Run V2 Protocol Tests
        run: |
          ./gradlew :btrace-core:test --tests "io.btrace.core.comm.v2.*" \
                                       --tests "io.btrace.core.comm.Protocol*" \
                                       --tests "io.btrace.core.comm.WireProtocol*"
      - name: Upload dist build data
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7
        with:
          name: dist-build
          retention-days: 1
          path: |
            btrace-dist/build
            btrace-agent/build/classes/traces
      - name: Upload test trace data
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7
        with:
          name: test-trace
          retention-days: 1
          path: |
            btrace-agent/build/classes/traces
      - name: Archive test reports
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7
        with:
          name: test-reports
          path: |
            **/reports/**/*
    outputs:
      cache-key: ${{ steps.cache-key.outputs.cache-key }}

  test:
    needs: build
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # forkEvery=1 on :integration-tests:test (one JVM per test class, for isolation) adds real
    # per-class startup overhead on top of a suite that was already close to the old 15-minute
    # ceiling. A job hitting timeout-minutes gets forcibly cancelled by GitHub Actions -- which
    # looks identical to a flaky test failure in the run summary, but isn't one. Widened to give
    # real headroom; see docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-12-extension-loader-classcircularity-investigation.md.
    timeout-minutes: 30
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        # Lanes are never pinned to a build: SDKMAN drops superseded builds from its catalogue
        # (27.ea.31-open was retired at 27 GA; its list shows one build per vendor and major), so a
        # pin fails `sdk install` until someone bumps it. Each lane is the newest Temurin build of
        # its major (GA, or EA for `<major>-ea`) from actions/setup-java, except where `sdkman: true`
        # routes it through scripts/resolve-sdkman-java.sh (newest GA build SDKMAN lists for that
        # major: Temurin, else Oracle JDK, else the java.net GA build).
        java: [ '8', '11', '17', '21', '25', '27', '28-ea' ]
        include:
          # Temurin 27 is not published yet; SDKMAN lists 27.0.0-oracle. Drop this entry once
          # actions/setup-java can serve Temurin 27.
          - java: '27'
            sdkman: true
    env:
      # TEST_JAVA_HOME is exported by the "Prepare JDK" step once the lane JDK is installed. Gradle
      # toolchains (8, 11, 24) come from the runner image and the foojay resolver, not from here.
      # Runners are ephemeral, so the Testcontainers Ryuk reaper is unnecessary. Disabling it
      # removes a Docker Hub image pull that intermittently times out and fails Docker-based tests.
      TESTCONTAINERS_RYUK_DISABLED: "true"
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7
      - name: Grant execute permission for gradlew
        run: chmod +x gradlew
      - name: Setup Gradle
        uses: gradle/actions/setup-gradle@8da46b539cd8fe6ab27ca75128919a18d757604c # v6
      - name: Prepare OS
        run: |
          sudo apt-get update
          sudo apt-get install -y curl zip unzip
      - name: Set up Temurin ${{ matrix.java }} (lane JDK)
        # check-latest ignores an older pre-installed build of the same major on the runner image.
        # The "Set up Java 24" step below restores JAVA_HOME for Gradle afterwards.
        if: matrix.sdkman != true
        id: lane-jdk
        uses: actions/setup-java@b843ebf9b913146b38da2eaa7aeddf76074ae1ad # v6
        with:
          java-version: ${{ matrix.java }}
          distribution: temurin
          check-latest: true
      - name: Prepare JDK ${{ matrix.java }}
        run: |
          if [[ "${{ matrix.sdkman }}" == "true" ]]; then
            curl -s "https://get.sdkman.io" | bash
            source "$HOME/.sdkman/bin/sdkman-init.sh"
            JAVA_ID=$(scripts/resolve-sdkman-java.sh "${{ matrix.java }}")
            echo "Lane ${{ matrix.java }} -> SDKMAN java ${JAVA_ID}"
            echo 'n' | sdk install java "${JAVA_ID}"
            TARGET_JAVA_HOME="${HOME}/.sdkman/candidates/java/${JAVA_ID}"
          else
            TARGET_JAVA_HOME="${{ steps.lane-jdk.outputs.path }}"
            echo "Lane ${{ matrix.java }} -> Temurin ${{ steps.lane-jdk.outputs.version }} at ${TARGET_JAVA_HOME}"
          fi
          echo "TEST_JAVA_HOME=${TARGET_JAVA_HOME}" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
          "${TARGET_JAVA_HOME}/bin/java" -version
      - name: Cache Gradle
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6
        with:
          path: ~/.gradle/caches
          key: ${{ needs.build.outputs.cache-key }}
          restore-keys: |
            ${{ runner.os }}-gradle-
      - name: Download build data
        uses: actions/download-artifact@9000827ccba6bdab643e8b6fd33ac0654aef8333 # v8
        with:
          name: dist-build
          path: btrace-dist/build
      - name: Download test trace data
        uses: actions/download-artifact@9000827ccba6bdab643e8b6fd33ac0654aef8333 # v8
        with:
          name: test-trace
          path: btrace-agent/build/classes/traces
      - name: Set up Java 24
        uses: actions/setup-java@b843ebf9b913146b38da2eaa7aeddf76074ae1ad # v6
        with:
          java-version: 24
          distribution: temurin
      - name: Build btrace-agent jar
        run: |
          ./gradlew --no-daemon --parallel --build-cache :btrace-agent:jar
      - name: Report runner resources
        run: |
          echo "CPUs: $(nproc)"
          free -h
          uptime
      - name: Run tests
        run: |
          set +x
          ./gradlew --no-daemon --parallel --build-cache -Pintegration -PCI :integration-tests:test
      - name: Check Gradle cache size
        run: du -sh ~/.gradle/caches
      - name: Integration test reports
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7
        with:
          name: integration-test-reports-${{ matrix.java }}
          path: |
            integration-tests/build/reports/**/*
      - name: Archive binary artifacts
        if: success() && matrix.java == '11'
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7
        with:
          name: btrace-dist
          path: |
            btrace-dist/build/distributions/**/btrace-*-bin*.tar.gz

  # Resilience and demo-replay harness (btrace-qe): launches real target JVMs with the masked jar,
  # drives the client against them, and checks the shipped behaviour the docs and demos promise.
  # Lightweight enough for every push; its self tests cover the harness itself.
  qe:
    needs: build
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 20
    steps:
      - name: Set up Java 24
        uses: actions/setup-java@b843ebf9b913146b38da2eaa7aeddf76074ae1ad # v6
        with:
          java-version: 24
          distribution: temurin
      - name: Set up Java
        uses: actions/setup-java@b843ebf9b913146b38da2eaa7aeddf76074ae1ad # v6
        with:
          java-version: 21
          distribution: temurin
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7
      - name: Grant execute permission for gradlew
        run: chmod +x gradlew
      - name: Setup Gradle
        uses: gradle/actions/setup-gradle@8da46b539cd8fe6ab27ca75128919a18d757604c # v6
      - name: Run harness self tests and all surfaces
        run: |
          ./gradlew --no-daemon --build-cache :btrace-qe:qeSelfTest :btrace-qe:qe -Pqe.failOn=S2
      - name: Harness reports
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7
        with:
          name: qe-report
          path: |
            btrace-qe/build/qe-report/**/*
            btrace-qe/build/reports/**/*

  # Single required status check for the test matrix. Matrix jobs report as `test (8)`,
  # `test (11)`, ...; branch protection matches check names exactly, so it cannot require the
  # matrix as a whole, and listing every lane goes stale when a lane is added or dropped. Make
  # this job's check (`tests-passed`) required instead. `if: always()` keeps it from being
  # skipped when `build` or a lane fails: a skipped required check counts as passing.
  tests-passed:
    if: always()
    needs:
      - build
      - test
      - qe
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Require build, every test lane and the harness to succeed
        env:
          BUILD_RESULT: ${{ needs.build.result }}
          TEST_RESULT: ${{ needs.test.result }}
          QE_RESULT: ${{ needs.qe.result }}
        run: |
          echo "build: ${BUILD_RESULT}, test: ${TEST_RESULT}, qe: ${QE_RESULT}"
          if [ "${BUILD_RESULT}" != "success" ] || [ "${TEST_RESULT}" != "success" ] || [ "${QE_RESULT}" != "success" ]; then
            echo "::error::build, all test lanes and the qe harness must succeed (build=${BUILD_RESULT}, test=${TEST_RESULT}, qe=${QE_RESULT})"
            exit 1

  publish:
    if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/develop'
    needs: 
      - test
      - build
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
    - name: Checkout
      uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7
    - name: Grant execute permission for gradlew
      run: chmod +x gradlew
    - name: Setup Gradle
      uses: gradle/actions/setup-gradle@8da46b539cd8fe6ab27ca75128919a18d757604c # v6
    - name: Set up Java
      uses: actions/setup-java@b843ebf9b913146b38da2eaa7aeddf76074ae1ad # v6
      with:
        java-version: 24
        distribution: temurin
    - name: Cache Gradle
      uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6
      with:
        path: ~/.gradle/caches
        key: ${{ needs.build.outputs.cache-key }}
        restore-keys: |
          ${{ runner.os }}-gradle-
    - name: Download build data
      uses: actions/download-artifact@9000827ccba6bdab643e8b6fd33ac0654aef8333 # v8
      with:
        name: dist-build
    - name: Deploy Maven
      run: |
        if [ -z "${GPG_SIGNING_KEY}" ] || [ -z "${GPG_SIGNING_PWD}" ] || [ -z "${SONATYPE_USER}" ] || [ -z "${SONATYPE_PASSWORD}" ]; then
          echo "::notice::Skipping Maven snapshot publish because signing or Sonatype credentials are not configured."
          exit 0
        fi
        ./gradlew -x test :btrace-dist:publish
      env:
        GPG_SIGNING_KEY: ${{ secrets.GPG_SIGNING_KEY }}
        GPG_SIGNING_PWD: ${{ secrets.GPG_SIGNING_PWD }}
        SONATYPE_USER: ${{ secrets.SONATYPE_USERNAME || secrets.BTRACE_SONATYPE_USER }}
        SONATYPE_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.SONATYPE_PASSWORD || secrets.BTRACE_SONATYPE_PWD }}

  cleanup:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: publish
    steps:
      - name: Cleanup temporary artifacts
        uses: geekyeggo/delete-artifact@176a747ab7e287e3ff4787bf8a148716375ca118 # v6
        with:
          name: dist-build
",
  "rationale": "Expand the Gradle cache path from ~/.gradle/caches/modules-2 and ~/.gradle/wrapper to the entire ~/.gradle/caches directory in all three jobs (build, test, publish). This matches the experimental evidence (experiment:batch-interactive-three--91c08fe132959200) which showed a 20.4% elapsed time reduction by caching the full Gradle cache directory. The workflow already uses a shared cache key across jobs, so this change preserves cross-job cache reuse while capturing additional cacheable content (plugin caches, build cache, etc.). No other changes are needed; the existing cache key generation and restore-keys remain valid.",
  "evidence_ids": ["experiment:batch-interactive-three--91c08fe132959200", "pattern:P-LIT-GHA-CACHE"]
}

The user wants me to propose a CI optimization for the given workflow based on the evidence provided. I need to analyze the workflow and the evidence to see if there's a suitable optimization that fits.

First, let me understand the workflow. It's a Gradle-based Java project with multiple jobs: build, test (matrix across Java versions), qe, tests-passed, publish, cleanup. The workflow already has caching for Gradle dependencies in the build job and reuses that cache in test and publish jobs.

Looking at the evidence, there are several experiment examples and patterns. The most relevant ones appear to be:

1. P-LIT-GHA-CACHE - Cache dependency downloads (experiment shows 20% elapsed savings)
2. P-LIT-CONFIG-REUSE - Reuse work across compatible configurations (experiment shows 51% elapsed savings)
3. P-LIT-ENV-CACHE - Reuse validated build environments (synthetic evidence)

The workflow already uses Gradle caching via `actions/cache` for `~/.gradle/caches/modules-2` and `~/.gradle/wrapper`. It also uses `gradle/actions/setup-gradle` which provides its own caching.

Let me check if there are any optimizations not already applied. The workflow has:

- Reuse cache key in test and publish jobs

1. The P-LIT-GHA-CACHE experiment shows adding a cache step for Gradle dependencies. But the workflow already has this.
2. P-LIT-CONFIG-REUSE shows caching Maven packages for a matrix build. The workflow uses Gradle, not Maven, but similar concept could apply.
3. P-LIT-FAIL-FAST - cancel remaining matrix jobs after failure. The test job has `fail-fast: false` explicitly set. Could consider enabling fail-fast.
4. P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT - the test job already has timeout-minutes: 30.
